thread:
sana: heads-up — I sketched a tiny RFC for surfacing kernel selection + KV-hit info directly on the per-request timeline. The goal: one-click jump from cost/latency chart to the exact request token ribbon.

michael: love it. is this just a dashboard overlay or do we need extra telemetry emitted from the runtime? :eyes:

sana: runtime needs minimal extra labels. proposal: when we emit per-request metrics, attach a short kernel fingerprint + KV-hit bitmap and a trace_id. Example log/metric fields: `request_id`, `trace_id`, `kernel_sha`, `kernel_mode`, `kv_hits_summary` (compressed), `token_count`.

jia: can you paste an example line? makes it easier to review.

sana: sure — sample structured log: ```json
{"ts":"...","request_id":"r-123","trace_id":"t-abc","kernel_mode":"int4-fused","kernel_sha":"k-9f2a","kv_hits_summary":"0,0,1,1,0","tokens":23,"lat_ms":42}```

eva: ok so the KV summary is an inline bitmap. smaller than full per-token arrays. but how do we map bitmap positions to token timeline in the UI?

sana: frontend: expand bitmap into a ribbon where green=KV-hit, gray=miss. the ribbon aligns with existing token-timeline. if user hovers a token, show kernel used for that token (if kernel switched mid-request), plus a link to the trace span.

ramon: switching kernels mid-request is realistic (small prompt -> switch to faster kernel). does runtime already emit kernel switches?

michael: not consistently. we currently log kernel selection events at kernel-change, but not attached to request-level metrics. need per-request annotation emitted when switch happens.

jia: perf-bot just flagged two regressions after the last kernel rollout — both were correlated to a kernel fallback path when batch size spiked. We should include `batch_context` in the metric too (batch_id, batch_size).

sana: agreed. updated telemetry fields: `request_id`, `trace_id`, `kernel_events` (list compressed like `t0:kA,t8:kB`), `kv_hits_summary`, `batch_size_hint`, `tokens`, `route`. Keep payload small.

perf-bot: FYI — recent rollouts: kernel k-9f2a -> k-4c01 at 1898000000. Two regressions detected: +8% p95 on /chat and +12% tail on /complete when batch_size>8.

eva: right — those p95 blips matched times when the runtime fell back to a generic attention kernel. If we can surface 'kernel_events' on the per-request view we can quickly see which requests experienced the fallback.

michael: operationally we want clickable links from the request row in dashboards -> trace explorer (jaeger/tempo). Suggested link format: `https://traces.redwood.local/trace/{trace_id}?span=request.{request_id}`. The runtime must include trace_id in the metric.

sana: UX note: add a compact per-route KPI on the route page: avg tokens/req, kv-hit-rate, p50/p95 latency, fraction of requests with kernel-fallback. each metric should be filterable by time-window and batch_size.

ramon: implementation plan? I can do runtime changes to emit the compressed `kernel_events` and `kv_hits_summary` in the metric export. frontend folks will map it to the ribbon.

jia: I'll own dashboard changes and the alert: `rate(kernel_fallback_count{route=\"/chat\"}[5m]) > 0.01` — want a canary alert that pages if >1% of requests fallback in 5m.

sana: QA: add a short e2e test that crafts requests forcing kernel fallback and asserts that the emitted `kernel_events` contains `fallback` for that request_id. Also verify trace link resolves.

eva: small concern about cardinality for batch_id and kernel_sha in metrics. prefer to keep kernel_sha as a tag only on traces/logs; in metrics use `kernel_class` (e.g., fused/int4/generic) to avoid high-cardinality.

sana: good call — update: `kernel_events` will use `kernel_class` and optional `kernel_tag` only for logs. So metrics stay low-card.

michael: timeline for rollout? Ramon + Jia pair next sprint, I'll schedule a short sig-release and add to eng-all-hands. If we see >0.5% fallback after rollout we'll rollback.

ramon: noted. I'll start a draft PR against runtime-exporter with the compressed schema and unit tests. Posting initial PR link when ready.

sana: thanks — next actions: ramon PR, jia dashboard patch + alert, michael release plan. Leaving a comment here when PR is up. :thumbsup:
